claim.why_it_matters: '## FORMAT 3' is the same heading rank as '## 14.9.22 INSPECT statement' (line 27762). Any heading-based section extraction over ISO_COBOL.md therefore terminates 14.9.22.4 General rules at rule 18 and re-parents General rules 19 through 23 (the entire normative definition of INSPECT formats 3 and 4, including EC-RANGE-INSPECT-SIZE for format 4) into two bogus top-level sections named 'FORMAT 3' and 'FORMAT 4'. A citation lookup for 14.9.22.4 GR 20 will silently miss it. The inconsistency is local and self-evident: the identical labels on the immediately preceding and following pages are plain text.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED on all three legs - printed typography, transcription inconsistency, and extraction impact - though the claim's line numbers are off by 3 and its 'kind' label is inverted.

1. PDF GLYPH EVIDENCE (rendered at 300 dpi, cropped and inspected directly). On page 680, 'FORMAT 3' and 'FORMAT 4' are set in the regular-weight serif body face at body size, flush to the same left margin as the numbered rules, with no bold and no size increase. Cropping each label together with the rule immediately below it shows 'FORMAT 3' and '19) A format 3 INSPECT statement is interpreted and executed...' sharing identical cap-height, stroke weight and stem contrast; same for 'FORMAT 4' and rule 20. For contrast, the running header 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' at the top of the same page IS bold, and every genuine heading in this standard is numbered (e.g. '14.9.22.4 General rules'). These two labels are unnumbered, unbolded, body-size text. I then rendered page 679 and cropped its 'FORMAT 1' label: it is typographically INDISTINGUISHABLE from page 680's 'FORMAT 3'/'FORMAT 4' - same face, weight, size, margin - yet the transcription leaves it as plain text (line 27988). Identical printed typography, two different markdown structures, so the transcription is self-refuting regardless of which reading one prefers; and the glyphs say plain body text.

2. TRANSCRIPTION INCONSISTENCY (verified, wider than claimed). Inside 14.9.22 every other applicability label is plain text: 'FORMATS 1 AND 3' (27876), 'FORMATS 2 AND 3' (27880), 'FORMAT 1' (27886), 'FORMAT 4' (27890), 'FORMATS 1 AND 2' (27932), 'FORMAT 1' (27988), 'FORMATS 2 AND 3' (28004), 'FORMAT 2' (28010). Only 28032 and 28036 carry '## '. Document-wide the ratio is stark: a grep for /FORMATS? [0-9]/ returns roughly 200 plain-text labels and exactly 8 lines prefixed with '##' - 6283, 6287, 6291, 6301, 19803, 25363, 28032, 28036. So the two lines under dispute are part of a recurring 8-instance defect class, not a one-off.

3. STRUCTURAL IMPACT (empirically reproduced, not merely argued). I did not take the impact claim on trust - I checked the repo's own consumer, scripts/spec/extract_rule_catalog.py. It defines ANY_HEADING = ^#{1,6}\s+\S and its main loop comment at line 163 states 'ANY heading closes the current rule block'. It filters only page furniture ahead of buffering: PAGE = ^##\s+Page\s+(\d+)\s*$ and RUNNING_HEADER = ^#{1,6}\s*(?:\*\*)?ISO/IEC\s+1989:2023\s*\(E\)(?:\*\*)?\s*$. '## FORMAT 3' matches ANY_HEADING and is caught by neither filter. Replaying that exact logic from the '## 14.9.22.4 General rules' heading, the block closes at line 28032 on '## FORMAT 3', having captured top-level ordinals 1 through 18 and nothing beyond. Orphaned past the cut: GR 19 (28034), GR 20 (28038), GR 21 (28040), GR 22 (28042, the EC-RANGE-INSPECT-SIZE size-equality requirement for format 4), GR 23 (28044). That is precisely the claimed loss - the whole normative definition of INSPECT formats 3 and 4 - and it terminates 'at rule 18' exactly as stated.

WHY THE STANDARD REJECTION GROUNDS DO NOT APPLY. Nothing is textually missing: both labels and all of GR 19-23 are present verbatim and correctly worded, so this is not lost text, reflow, wrapping, hyphenation or a page-break artifact. Nor is it dismissible as 'only formatting': in a markdown transcription the ATX heading level IS the encoded document structure, and I demonstrated by execution that this particular formatting choice changes which normative rules the repo's rule-catalog extractor attributes to 14.9.22.4. It also cannot be excused as the pipeline honoring some invisible cue - the labels are unnumbered and appear in no table of contents, and their printed form is identical to siblings the same pipeline rendered as plain text.
verdict.corrected_description:
REAL, but the ledger entry mislabels the defect and miscites its lines.

(a) Direction is inverted. kind should be 'spurious-heading' / 'over-promoted-heading', not 'missing-heading'. No heading is missing and no text is missing; two lines of ordinary body text were wrongly promoted to level-2 ATX headings. The claim's own prose ('promoted to level-2 ATX headings') is accurate - only the kind label contradicts it.

(b) Every line number in the claim is 3 too low. Actual: '## FORMAT 3' is at line 28032 (claimed 28029); '## FORMAT 4' at 28036 (claimed 28033); '## 14.9.22 INSPECT statement' at 27765 (claimed 27762); the plain-text 'FORMAT 2' at 28010 (claimed 28007).

(c) The truncation collision is nearer than described. The heading whose block actually gets cut is '## 14.9.22.4 General rules' at line 27895 - which is itself anomalously '##' where its sibling '### 14.9.21.4 General rules' (line 27738) is '###'. Naming '## 14.9.22 INSPECT statement' as the rank-peer is true but indirect; the operative peer is the General rules heading two levels down that shares the same '##' rank.

(d) Scope is broader than one page. The same over-promotion recurs at 6 further sites in specs/ISO_COBOL.md - lines 6283 ('## FORMAT 1'), 6287 ('## FORMAT 2'), 6291 ('## FORMAT 3'), 6301 ('## FORMAT 4'), 19803 ('## FORMAT 4') and 25363 ('## FORMAT 3') - against roughly 200 correctly-plain FORMAT labels. The fix should demote all 8, not just the two on page 680.

(e) Impact confirmed by execution, and worth recording as such: replaying extract_rule_catalog.py's ANY_HEADING/PAGE/RUNNING_HEADER logic truncates 14.9.22.4 General rules after GR 18, orphaning GR 19-23 including GR 22's EC-RANGE-INSPECT-SIZE size-equality requirement for format 4.
